page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose virtual instance based on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor, the instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs originating from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes no bundled local storage, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage. Networking capabilities are anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution, driven by modern AMD Zen core architecture, placing both stress-ng single-core (3111.39) and Geekbench single-core (2006.0) scores in the upper 25th percentile. Large-block memory bandwidth is stable at 47.71 GB/sec for reads and 27.73 GB/sec for writes. However, overall aggregate throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU ceiling: PassMark CPU (3861.67) and Geekbench multi-core (2501.0) scores settle in the lower quartile, with database operations and static web serving also ranking low.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance delivers resource efficiency for workloads bound by single-core speed rather than scale-out parallel computation. The lack of integrated storage necessitates accounting for block storage overhead. Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance and solid single-thread capacity, Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is suited for low-traffic web applications, lightweight backend utilities, intermediate microservices, and development environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, driven by a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor on KVM architecture. Built on a single physical core with two execution threads, it includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local storage, relying on external network block storage, and operates with a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows strong single-core computational performance in both stress-ng and Geekbench, though total multi-core execution and database throughput are naturally constrained by the dual-vCPU capacity. Memory read and write metrics maintain solid average throughput. With its balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, this instance is suited for lightweight web serving, application staging, microservices, and single-thread-intensive utility tasks.
